art.title: Riftbound World Showcase
art.desc: We’re announcing the format and prizing for the Riftbound World Showcase.
art.html:
Riftbound had an explosive first year, and we’re excited to conclude the inaugural competitive season in style with the World Showcase happening January 22-23, 2027, in Shanghai, China. The world’s best Riftbounders will battle it out for the glory of becoming the first Riftbound World Champion. 

Riftbound’s next set, Legacy, doesn’t release until January 29, one week after the event—but to push competitors to their limits and delight viewers, World Showcase competitors will get to play with the set. 

Competitors in the event will get early access to the complete Legacy card list two weeks before the event (which will be before previews are completed for the community). Additionally, competitors will have to register and compete with three separate constructed decks, which must be built without overlapping Domains. 

Riftbound World Showcase - Event Details

Date: January 22-23, 2027 

Location: Shanghai, China

Where to Watch: Twitch │YouTube

Deckbuilding

Competitors will get early access to the Legacy card list. They’ll have to build three decks (Deck A, Deck B, Deck C) with the following requirements:

  • No overlapping Domains between the three decks.
  • One deck must be designated during registration as their “Playoff Deck.” 
    • They will use the designated deck in the Top 4.

Pairings

At the World Showcase, competitors will play 9 rounds of Swiss matches before reaching the top 4. In Swiss matches, competitors will use Deck A for rounds 1-3, Deck B for rounds 4-6, and Deck C for rounds 7-9.

While using Deck A in the first rounds, competitors will not be matched against the same opponent in multiple games. Once competitors transition to playing Deck B or Deck C in later rounds, they may be matched against an opponent they have already played.

Day 1 (Swiss)

Day 2 (Swiss/Top 4)

Day 2 (Top 4)

Rounds 1-3: Deck A

Rounds 4-6: Deck B

Rounds 7-9: Deck C

Single Elimination

Best-of-3 matches

Playoff Deck

Prizing

Riftbounders who have ascended to the pinnacle of competition deserve a fitting reward for their hard work. Check out the prizing details below:

  • An all expenses paid trip to China for the competition.
  • A premium competitor goodie bag.
  • Exclusive serialized English promo numbered 1-24 (matching the total number of competitors), distributed based on final standings.
  • $100k USD total prize pool.
  • World Champion trophy.
  • OVN Foil Plated Legends drafted based on final standing.
    • All Legends including Legacy will be available to draft.
    • This will differ from the Regional Championship Overnumber Foil Plated Legends and will not have a promo stamp. 

Keep an eye on our social channels @PlayRiftbound and @RiftboundOP for updates, and good luck to all of the competitors heading into our Regional Championships!

art.title: All Eyes on RC Europe
art.desc: The best of Riftbound gather in Stuttgart, Germany!
art.html:
The penultimate tournament of 2026 Riftbound Organized Play is happening soon in Stuttgart, Germany next month! After a year of battling through RQs, the Riftbound Regional Championship: Europe will be the region’s largest event yet. Stuttgart continues to elevate the ultimate community experience with exclusive prizing, all new side events like Nation Clash, on-site card grading, free popcorn and so much more.

RC EU Venue Info

Event Location

Messe Stuttgart
Messepiazza 1
70629 Stuttgart
Germany
Hall 8 + 10

Hours

All times in Stuttgart Time (CET)

  • Badge Collection: 2:00 PM – 7:00 PM

  • Badge Collection: 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM
  • Hall Hours: 8:30 AM – 11:00 PM (Premium attendees can enter starting at 8:00 AM)

Sunday

  • Hall Hours: 8:30 AM – 8:00 PM (Premium attendees can enter starting at 8:00 AM)

What’s on the Line?

Legends will be made, rivalries will be settled, and a new champion will emerge. With $50,000 on the line, Europe’s fiercest competitors will battle for the ultimate distinction: the title of Riftbound European Regional Champion.

Along the way, players will have the opportunity to earn exclusive promos and rewards, including coveted Overnumbered Foil Plated Legends. For the Top 8, the stakes climb even higher, with invitations to Riftbound’s first World Championship Showcase and the chance to represent Europe among the world’s best.

Only one player will claim the crown and etch their name into Riftbound history.

Season 5 RC EU Prizing

  • 1st Place: $10,000, Champion Card, Champion Playmat
  • 2nd Place: $5,000
  • 3rd/4th: $2,500
  • 5th-8th: $1,500
  • 9th-16th: $1,000
  • 17th-32nd: $500
  • 33rd-64th: $250

You can find a full breakdown of prizing in our Regional Championship Info article.

Overnumbered Foil Plated Legends

The European Regional Championship raises the stakes with Overnumbered Foil Plated Legends awarded based on overall tournament performance. The top 58 competitors will each draft a card from the available pool, starting with the champion and proceeding in placement order until all 58 Legends have been selected.

Riftbound x Worlds 2026 Edition

You’ll be able to snag one of the Worlds 2026 Bundles at RC Europe. Details on purchasing will be sent to attendees.

Contents

  • 1 collectible Legend promo card, featuring new art exclusively for Worlds.
    • Unforgiven (Yasuo).
  • 3 collectible Battlefield promo cards, featuring art of each Worlds 2026 host city.
    • Los Angeles, Allen, and New York City.
  • 1 Worlds 2026 Deck Box.
  • 1 pack of Worlds 2026 Foil Card Sleeves.

Live Grading at RC Europe

We’re teaming up with Premiere Card Grading to give attendees an opportunity to grade a piece of Riftbound history!

Choose from three slab options that include an exclusive Riftbound Regional Championship 2026 label! Whether you pull a grail on the show floor or bring a prized card from home, the PCG team is ready to help you protect your collection and commemorate the event.

  • Grading Options: Same-Day (limited capacity), Next-Day, and Standard grading with tracked return shipping within Europe.
  • Exclusive Features: Eligible Riftbound cards can receive an exclusive Regional Championship 2026 label developed in partnership with Riot at no extra cost.
  • Commemorative Packaging: Every submission will be returned in a special Regional Championship Gold foil box created alongside Riot—a perfect keepsake from the event.

Coverage Information

Follow the action all weekend long on Riftbound’s YouTube and Twitch channels.

You can catch the action live starting at:

  • 10:00 AM CET
  • 1:00 AM PST
  • 8:00 AM GMT

Our desk will feature:

  • Hosts: Amy Wosley & Barcode
  • Play-by-Play: James O'Leary, Shai Burton, Lothar
  • Color commentators: Leonard Köning & Riftbound Senior Designer Aaron Barich

Watch live on Riftbound’s YouTube and Twitch channels. Make sure you’re following so you don’t miss the opening match.

Reaction-Speed Coverage on @RiftboundOP

Following on the go? @RiftboundOP on X will have coverage throughout the weekend.

What you can expect:

  • Match Results
  • Bracket Updates
  • Player Interviews
  • Behind-the-Scenes Content
  • Deck Techs

@RiftboundOP is also your year-round home for Riftbound Organized Play, covering everything from Nexus Nights and Summoner Skirmish Series to Regional Qualifiers, Championships, and Worlds.

Rules Hub

Want to make sure you’re ready for Stuttgart?

Visit the newly updated Rules Hub for the latest rules, regulations, and gameplay systems. Whether you’re double-checking interactions or reviewing tournament structure, this is your go-to resource heading into the weekend.

In Closing

Anticipation is reaching an all-time high as the 2026 season of Riftbound OP comes to a close. Whether you’re gearing up to meet your favorite creators, talk strategy, dive into a casual match, or make Riftbound history, it’s all waiting for you in Stuttgart.

Regional Championships:

  • Regional Championship: Europe - Stuttgart, Germany, Messe Stuttgart, Nov 6-8, 2026
    • Read more here: 2026 Regional Championship Info
    • Check out the hub: European Regional Championship Hub
  • Riftbound Regional Championship: North America at Convergence Fest - Las Vegas, NV, USA, Dec 11-13, 2026
    • You can register to spectate at Convergence Fest here!

The Riot and UVS teams will be onsite throughout the weekend, so we hope to hear from you. Let’s chat Riftbound together!

Above all, we want to say thank you. This space continues to grow and turn more players into legends because of your passion and dedication to the game. The Riftbound community continues to inspire everything we do, and we appreciate each player whether you’re joining us at your LGS or the global stage.

art.title: Radiance Rules FAQ and Clarifications
art.desc: Answers for some frequent questions about Radiance interactions.
art.html:
Welcome to the Radiance FAQ article! As mentioned in the Radiance Release Notes article, the FAQ article serves as a collection of rulings and clarifications at our usual cadence, and serves as an additional supplemental article to the Release Notes article.

The FAQ is a collection of official rulings. In places where the FAQ differs from the Core Rules Document, the FAQ takes precedence. When a new Core Rules Document is released, it will take precedence over any points that differ from this document. 

Throughout this document, we use some specific shorthand to represent symbols in card text. Here’s a short guide:

  • [E] means “exhaust”
  • [M] means “Might”
  • [A] means “one power of any domain”
  • [C] means “one power of this card’s domain”
    • [C] in Accelerate costs takes on the domain of the Unit, or turns into [A] if the Unit has no domain or multiple domains.
    • [C] in other cases is treated as the corresponding power symbol in all respects, matching how the cards are actually printed—it’s just a design shorthand!

—

If my opponent empowers Kharox and chooses to play my Neeko, Blending In from my trash with the triggered ability, do they get one of the Legends I chose during deckbuilding?

No.

When the play effect of the Neeko played through Kharox resolves, if their deck has one or more copies of Neeko, Blending In, they can add one of the Legends they chose during deckbuilding to their Legend Zone as if they had played a copy of Neeko that they own. The Legends they add to the Legend Zone don’t have any relation to the Legends their opponent chose. If their deck has no copies of Neeko, in the Main Deck or the sideboard, that instruction will be ignored.

If I play Mobilize while I control Seraphic Wyvern and I only have one rune left in my Rune Deck, do I still draw a card?

No.

Referencing the action in this way refers only to the game action and the game object it was performed on. The channel event that Seraphic Wyvern instructs introduces a new game object that the action is performed on, but the referenced action is still only the original one in the instructions of the spell.

The same logic applies to Catalyst of Aeons played while its controller has a Seraphic Wyvern on the board and only two runes left in their Rune Deck. They were able to channel 2 runes, even if the additional game object instructed to be channeled by Seraphic Wyvern wasn’t possible. Therefore they will not draw 1.

Relevant rules: 359.3.e.14.c.

If I play Meticulous Restorationist from my trash for [Y] via its triggered ability, can I banish a unit or gear from my trash with Mordekaiser, Iron Revenant to pay the cost?

Yes.

“Play me for [Cost]” is an alternate cost which replaces the base cost ([2]) with the alternate cost ([Y]). Mordekaiser, Iron Revenant’s Power can only be spent to play units.

Relevant rules: 356.1.a.

If I play Atakhan and kill a non-token unit for its additional cost, can I banish that unit with Mordekaiser, Iron Revenant to help pay for Atakhan’s Power cost?

No.

When paying costs in Riftbound, you pay Energy and Power costs before you perform other “non-standard” costs, like Atakhan’s optional additional cost to kill a unit. When paying the Power cost of Atakhan, the unit in question is not actually dead yet, and thus cannot be banished from your trash.

Relevant rules: 357.1., 357.2.

If I kill Runeblade Anvil during an opponent’s turn, when is the last moment I can play the banished card?

You can play it until the Ending Phase in your next turn begins.

If I kill Runeblade Anvil during my turn, can I play the card during the Ending Phase of that turn?

No.

The duration for Runeblade Anvil’s permission is “until your next Ending Phase.” It is valid until the specified point in the specified turn begins, and then the permission is lost.

If I kill Runeblade Anvil during my Ending Phase, when is the last moment I can play the banished card?

You can play it until the Ending Phase in your next turn begins.

Your next Ending Phase after your current Ending Phase is the one in your next turn. Until that Ending Phase begins, you will be able to play the card in question.

If I control Hunters’ Circle and I play Baron Nashor without a Baron Pit on the board, can I play him for [9][C][C][C]?

Yes.

Hunters’ Circle applies a cost reduction to the first unit or gear each player plays there during their turn. Baron Nashor entering at the Baron Pit is a replacement effect that applies while Baron resolves and enters the board. In comparison, Hunters’ Circle’s cost reduction is in effect during finalization, when choosing play locations in step 2 and determining the total cost in step 3. By the time Baron Nashor’s replacement effect applies, his cost has been determined and paid.

Relevant rules: 355.2.

If I control a battlefield and I have Riven, the Exile as my legend, can I play Baron Nashor without a Baron Pit on the board and have him enter ready?

Yes.

Riven, the Exile applies a replacement effect to units her controller plays to a battlefield they control. This refers to step 2 of finalization, when players pick the play location for a unit they are playing. Riven then generates a replacement effect for those units, which causes them to enter ready. When Baron Nashor enters in this scenario, there are two replacement effects that apply to the event of him entering: him entering ready, and him entering to the Baron Pit. Regardless of the order of these replacement effects, Baron Nashor will enter ready at the Baron Pit.

Relevant rules: 355.2.

For Riven, Broken Blade’s exhaust trigger, do I spend the buff when finalizing the triggered ability or when it resolves?

When it resolves.

A cost within instructions that doesn’t appear as the first part of a triggered ability’s effect is part of the instructions that occur on resolution and not the base cost of the triggered ability. The first part of Riven, Broken Blade’s triggered ability is “Choose one that hasn’t been chosen this turn…”

Relevant rules: 383.3.b.

If I Standard Move a Riven, Broken Blade and a Stellacorn Herder simultaneously, which goes on the chain first: Riven’s exhaust trigger or Stellacorn Herder’s move trigger?

The exhaust trigger.

The order of the triggers on the chain after the move event completes is: exhaust triggers first, followed by move triggers. The cost to perform the move occurs before the move action is actually performed.

Relevant rules: 203.

If I attempt to Standard Move to a battlefield with Gravity Field and decline the cost, can I still exhaust my unit?

No.

The Standard Move is an inherent ability. We’ll clarify some established consensus on how the Standard Move operates: you cannot attempt to perform the Standard Move if the resulting move is not possible, nor if you cannot pay its associated costs.

Additionally, if the Standard Move incurs a Cost that cannot be paid, or if the move action cannot otherwise be performed, the Standard Move and all actions taken as part of performing it will be undone, any effects those actions caused to occur are similarly undone, and the Standard Move will be cancelled.

If I play Charm moving an enemy unit to a battlefield where I control Gravity Field, does its controller have to pay the cost?

No.

The opponent must pay [1][A] to move a unit to the battlefield with Gravity Field, but Charm instructs you to move the enemy unit and not your opponent.

If your opponent controlled the Gravity Field at that battlefield, you would be the one who would have to pay [1][A] to move the enemy unit to that battlefield when Charm resolves.

Relevant rules: 412.2. and its subrules

What about if I play Angler Wyrm’s activated ability while it’s located at the same battlefield with Gravity Field? Will they have to pay the cost to move the unit to the battlefield?

Yes.

Unlike Charm, Angler Wyrm instructs your opponent to move their unit, so they must pay the cost in order to move it to that battlefield. If they choose not to or can’t, the unit does not move.

Relevant rules: 412.2. and its subrules, 204.4., 204.4.b., 204.4.c. 

Speaking of Angler Wyrm, if my opponent plays Angler Wyrm’s activated ability choosing me and I play Hunker Down on one of my units, can I pick that unit when Angler Wyrm instructs me to move a unit even if I control other units?

No, you cannot.

The chosen opponent must perform the move game action if they have a unit that can move. If they control some number of units that cannot move, they cannot choose to “move” those units to satisfy the move instructions, as no move is actually possible. If they control no units that can move, the instruction is negated. If they have some number of units that can move, they must move one of those units.

If I play Possession and take control of my opponent’s Ekko, Revolutionary, can I play his activated ability to banish and then play him? Do I control him when he comes back in?

Yup and yup.

Relevant rules: 378., 191.2.

art.desc: The revamped 2027 Local Play program, including Nexus Cups, Challenge Series, and unused Byes.
art.html:
With Legacy on the horizon, we're taking a deeper dive into the upcoming programs for you to join at your local game store. As Riftbound grows and we have seen more about how you play and want to play, we will re-evaluate and improve our play programs.

Our vision for Riftbound play is to build two play programs which help us serve the different types of players in Riftbound: a Competitive ladder that serves players striving to compete and a separate structure that we've cleverly named 'Fun-petitive' to provide a structure that rewards players for being active at their local game stores and is less about the drive to win and more about the drive to socialize and participate.

At the core, good play programs are about incentivizing and rewarding players for playing the way they want to play, and we feel Riftbound is served best by building both of these tracks.

This isn't to say these are two separate pools of players. While you may be drawn to one or the other, there are certainly times the streams will cross, and you will be able to play in both. Good communities thrive on the diversity of their players.

Pre-Rift events will remain a staple of our play programs. The Legacy Pre-Rifts will kick off January 22, 2026, and run through January 28, 2026. Pre-Rifts will fall primarily in the Fun-petitive side of the play programs, but we have no doubt players who are driven by mastery will join alongside players who are looking to just hang and play some card games.

Summoner Skirmish Sunset & Bye-Back Details

Compare this to the soon-to-be sunset Summoner Skirmish program. As we shared in the State of Play article, this program was found to be in an awkward position. It had great promos and cool playmats our social players wanted to chase, but also Byes that our most competitive players were driven to farm. The mixed incentives, combined with the challenges we outlined around the bye-reward program, led us to rethink our store programs and land on the new Nexus Cup & Challenge Series programs.

With the announcement of Summoner Skirmish's coming retirement, we shared that we were working on plans for any unused Byes that you earned but were unable to use. We've got that update for you here.

If you have any unused Summoner Skirmish byes you will be able to redeem them at any Regional in 2027. You can do so by contacting UVS after registering for the event and emailing OP@uvsgames.com. The UVS support team will be able to implement this bye for you ahead of the event. Emails must be sent no later than 14 days prior to the start of the event. You can also implement the bye on-site at the event when you pick up your badge, ahead of the start of the main event.

If you cannot, or do not want to redeem any earned byes, we will be offering to replace them with a promo from Set 7, The Reckoning. We will be sharing it with players in the future when we open the redemption for this promo next year.

We'll be back with more information about how it will work as we get closer, but we do have answers for some of your most important questions about this program now:

  1. Byes will be redeemed 1-for-1 with the promo (multiple byes receive multiple promos).
  2. This promo will only be available via this redemption program.
  3. Redemptions will need to be completed by December 31, 2027, at 11:59:59pm Pacific.

-

Now, on to the new programs launching in January with Legacy.

Nexus Cup

Nexus Cup asks the question "Who's the local champion?" This is a per-set event at LGS aimed at crowning your store's best. The Nexus Cup doesn't feed up into the competitive programs; it's about local recognition and bragging rights.

While we did reveal the promo from The Reckoning, we aren't going to be revealing any Legacy promos today. What we can share is that the prizing for Nexus Cup will look like the following:

Prizing will look familiar to Summoner Skirmish players in that the promos will be:

  • Winner & Top 8 promos - Sharing the same card, with unique stamps to denote the placement
  • Winner playmat
  • Participation promos - A unique promo for players who compete in the event.

As we note in the other article today about the play programs, we are working on a 'Fun-petitive' play program, we'll share more details on that in the future.

Challenge Series

This is a per-set program which will be available to select Riftbound Gaming Network stores. As this directly feeds into the competitive ladder, we want to maintain a certain bar for stores to meet to qualify to run these events so as to give players the best experience and minimize issues as they begin their ascent up the ranked ladder.

If you haven't read it yet, be sure to read the other article today as it will give a much deeper overview of the competitive program, introduce Ladder Points, and dive into the benefits it affords as players rise in the ranks. We won't delve deeply into the details of it here, but here's a quick introduction.

Ladder Points are the points players earn as part of competitive Riftbound events. Ladder Points raise your rank on the Ladder, and each rank awards you benefits. You earn Ladder Points based on your finish in competitive events. Challenge Series award Ladder Points if you finish in the Top 32 of the event.

As 2026 made clear, many of you are hungry for the competitive challenges of Riftbound, and the Challenge Series is to help fill that demand.

Challenge Series events will award both promos and Challenge Points to competitors. For the launch of this series the rewards will look as follows:

These promos will be of the same card with unique stamps to denote a winner vs a Top 8 finisher. As with the Nexus Cup, we aren't ready to reveal the promo for this yet, hang in there.

Since we're sharing a great deal about the organized player programs for 2027 in this and the other article, we know you have questions and the community will raise issues to address. Stay tuned for updates or follow-ups based on the community conversations.

art.title: Riftbound 2027 Premier Play
art.desc: An overview of the revamped Premier Play program for 2027.
art.html:
August’s State of Play gave a high-level overview of the types of events that make up our 2027 Organized Play program. Today’s article is a behemoth with a lot of information about the updates to Riftbound’s play systems.

Here’s a quick summary of what’s in this article:

  1. Riftbound Organized Play is continuing to grow in 2027!
  2. Riftbound is getting a ranked ladder in 2027, and our top players of each year will earn the “Grandmaster” title.
  3. Our four Continentals in 2027 are in Dallas, Melbourne, London, and Toronto.
  4. Winners of Challenge Series events will earn a free competitor badge to a Regional.
  5. You can earn a competitor badge and qualify for Day 2 of Continentals through consistent top finishes at tournaments, even if they don’t earn a badge or invite directly from those tournaments.

There is a lot in this article—the above five things just scratch the surface. This article is one part primer on the system and one part introductory policy document. We’ve opted to go in-depth here to fully explain each change.

There is also a recurring point in this article that things are not finalized. We’re estimating our status to be… roughly 92.6%. What is that number based on? Nothing scientific. 

Part of the reason for this is because the Organized Play program is made up of a lot of separate parts and systems that all work together. For example, this article talks about how you can qualify for specific events, which means we have to get into both the events they can qualify for and the events they play in to earn that qualification. 

Given the size of this article, we broke out a separate article to talk specifically about the Nexus Cup & Challenge Series tournaments. That article also includes more details about the plans to sunset Summoner Skirmish, and what you can do with any byes they’ve earned but don’t plan to use at Regionals next year. We’ll discuss Challenge Series here as well, but mainly with respect to how it connects to the larger play program.

Now, before diving in: if you’d like a refresher, here’s a reminder about our core philosophy for Riftbound Organized Play. Skip ahead to the next section if you want to get right into the changes.

One Community. More Ways to Play.

This is our core philosophy for Riftbound’s play programs. 

We’re just a bit shy of 11 months since we held our first RQ in Houston. It’s no secret that Riftbound’s first year has exceeded our expectations in the best ways possible. Where our first year was about providing events for players; next year is about providing a more robust ecosystem for playing Riftbound.

To do that, as we spoke about during State of Play, we look at our tournaments and events as part of two types of play events: Competitive and ‘FUN-petitive’. The distinction between these categories is about the goal of the events and the types of players they are rewarding. All players can play on both sides of this divider, but this distinction is important for us as we design the systems around our play programs.

Competitive events are designed to attract and reward players for, among other things, competing, winning to score points, and standing in victory over their opponents. 

Fun-petitive events should have systems which are, well, fun. They should attract and reward players beyond those who are grinding for points. These players want to play the game and socialize with others. Sure, they may be excited to score the winning point, but also aren’t unhappy if they just got to use their favorite deck for a few games, win or lose (but probably win).

Both are completely valid reasons to play the game, and as such, we’re trying to build our programs to serve both in their own ways.

The paths converge at the most popular store events each set: Pre-Rift Prerelease events and Nexus Nights. These events serve a good combination of both Competitive and Fun-petitive players. Above them, we see the paths diverge.

But, no matter the tournament or event, we get to enjoy the beautiful thing about being a physical Trading Card Game: how Riftbound connects us with others.

Sometimes that connection is fleeting, just existing for the short time that we are sitting across from each other playing a game; other times it is lifelong, such as the bond between a play group that gets together regularly and plays games while telling stories and hanging out together. 

Others play as a by-product of their fandom of a certain element of Riftbound, like a specific Legend or Champion, the world of Runeterra, or another part of the League of Legends IP. 

This is not to say that you are only a real Riftbound fan if you attend events in person. Far from it. We get that life, geography, and responsibility sometimes makes that difficult.

Whatever the reason you’re part of the game, our goal is for there to be some tournament or event for you to enjoy.

By the nature of the program’s needs for 2027, the Competitive side has more complexity going on, and we’re going to spend most of today discussing it in-depth to give players a good understanding of what the competitive event landscape looks like next year.

2027's Competitive Program

To introduce our plans for 2027, we need to start with an explanation of what we're currently doing for Riftbound's competitive program and why we're changing.

2026 was built as a straightforward system of direct pathing and qualification:

  • Winning Summoner Skirmish gave you a bye at a Regional Qualifier.
  • Finishing Top 64 at a Regional Qualifier earned you an invite for a Regional Championship.
  • Being in the Top 8 at a Regional Championship gets you an invite to the 2026 World Championship Showcase.

It is a program built out of our need for speed; getting up and running during Riftbound's first year.

One of our frustrations with this program is that it defines players' results solely by their top finishes. If you consistently finish outside of the top ranks, you're out of luck; no matter how many times you come close. Until you break through, you may as well not have played. Enjoy your set of steak knives. (This is a movie reference. Neither Riot nor UVS offer steak knives as prizing... Yet?)

For 2027 we are introducing a number of changes which improve the system, starting with two things most gamers are familiar with: Ladder Points and a Ranked Ladder for competitive events.

Ladder Points

Ladders are nothing new, especially for Riot. In 2027, every competitive event you play will give you a chance to earn Ladder Points (LP), rewarded based on how you finish. Those ladder points determine your level on Riftbound's Ranked Ladder.

Let's take a look at how we're planning to distribute Ladder Points based on finishes in competitive events.

Important notes:

  • We are fairly confident these point values will hold, but this is something which we may still adjust between now and the beginning of 2027.
  • For multi-day events such as Regionals and Continentals, you must make Day 2 to earn any points. If they do, they will receive a minimum of 10 points.
  • There is a mathematically unlikely situation where if someone finishes a Regional or Continental such that they would receive points by their standing, but it isn’t enough to make Day 2, they will receive zero points instead.

The LP you earn accumulates to form your Ladder rank. The rank is not just about bragging rights; it also will bring some benefits, such as early registration for Regionals, but more on that later in this article. As soon as you attain a rank, you unlock some of those benefits immediately, and you’ll have them for the current year and through the following year. However, the rank must be maintained to keep your benefits past that.

For example: If you reach Gold in June of 2027, you will immediately become Gold on the Ranked Ladder. When Ladder points reset for 2028, you will retain your Gold benefits. But if at the end of 2028 you have only reached Silver on the Ladder, you will lose Gold benefits, and you’ll have Silver benefits heading into 2029 when the Ladder Points reset again. 

Ranked Ladder

The Ranked Ladder has five levels (with a secret sixth one…) We aren’t ready to share the Ladder Point thresholds for each rank, but to help give context on how we view this Ladder, we’re sharing the estimated population size for each rank.

Two notes for the next table:

  1. The estimated population in the right column speaks to our intent with this system. It is not a cap or a definition; it is meant to show the general shape of the rank sizes we are envisioning.
  2. These percentage estimates are representative of players who are actively engaging in the competitive play programs and the ladder and not the overall player population as a whole.
Aspirant~11% of players
Bronze~50% of players
Silver~33% of players
Gold~5% of players
Platinum~1% of players

We aren’t ready to share the complete list of benefits that each rank will receive, but you can expect to see exclusive Promos and other unique swag as the ranks grow.

One benefit that we are ready to share with you comes for the top two ranks: Gold & Platinum. Gold or Platinum ranks will have access to a priority registration window for Regionals and Continentals.

Priority Registration for Regionals & Continentals

Every Regional and Continental will have their competitor badges split into two pools. (Note we’re exclusively discussing competitor badges for these events.)

  • Pool A: competitor badges for purchase by the full Riftbound community.
  • Pool B: competitor badges used to fulfill badge needs through qualifications to the event and priority registration windows.

The general structure for this will be that the Pool B portion of the competitor badges will provide competitor badges to everyone who has earned a competitor badge for the event directly, or who has redeemed a “token” for this event.

We go into more detail about what tokens are later in the article, but we will be mentioning them a few more times before the full explanation. The simplified definition is that they are a type of invitation for those who earn them, which gives the player choices on when to redeem them.

Badges remaining in Pool B will also be made available through the early registration windows. 48 hours prior to tickets going on sale for the community, they will be sold to Platinum rank players. 24 hours later they will be sold to Gold rank players. Unsold Pool B badges will be combined with Pool A’s competitor badges for the broader community sale.

The method of badge sales for Pool A badges is something we are also still working on. This is not meant to be us presenting the ultimate solution to the frustrations experienced when purchasing event badges this year.

Top Finish Races

We opted not to have your Ladder rank directly qualify you for Continentals or provide badges for Regionals, because doing so incentivizes you to play every possible event. Instead, we’re introducing “Top Finish Races.” Essentially, these are leaderboards which only count your top finishes at events filtered with specific restrictions.

Across specific sets of time, only certain numbers of top finishes from certain types of events are counted. There are two types of Top Finish Race: ‘Seasonal’ and ‘Annual.’ Seasonal refers to a time going from set release to set release, and Annual refers to the calendar year.

This approach promotes healthier play patterns as it allows players who achieve good results to not have to continue competing in every tournament. Essentially, it’s our attempt to find the balance between these races being about quality of finish and not quantity.

So what do the Annual and Seasonal Top Finish Races get me?

Seasonal Top Finish Race

The Seasonal Top Finish Race resets with the launch of each new Riftbound set. At that time, we will award Continental Day 2 tokens to the Top 50 players in the Seasonal Top Finish Race who did not already receive a Continental Day 2 token during that same set through other means. As noted earlier, we will explain ‘tokens’ in more depth soon, for now think of them as an invitation which allows you some agency to choose which event you attend with that invitation.

The Seasonal Top Finish score is calculated by taking the following best results for your:

  • Best 3 Challenge Series or Showdown Series ladder point results.
  • Best Regional or Continental ladder point result.

Example Seasonal Point Race Result

In the following example, a player has six tournament results that award them Ladder Points, which are relevant for a Seasonal Top Finish race. The bolded rows are the ones which are counted:

Your Seasonal Top Finish score would be: (18 + 30 + 35) + (40) = 123 points. 

With The Reckoning’s release, the system will look at the top players in the Seasonal Top Finish race right before it resets. It will look only for players who don’t already have a Continental Day 2 token, and it will award the Top 50 of those players a Continental Day 2 token.

Annual Top Finish Race

The Annual Top Finish Race follows the above framework, combining the same two groups of finishes, but extends the relevant time period and collects results from more events across the year:

  • Best 12 Challenge Series or Showdown Series ladder point results.
  • Best 5 Regional or Continental ladder point results.

Those 17 results are added together to determine your Annual Top Finish score, which can earn you invitations to Worlds and, potentially, a Grandmaster title.

At the conclusion of the Annual Top Finish Race:

  • The Top 50 players in each Annual Top Finish Race will be awarded the title of Grandmaster.
  • Additionally, starting for 2027’s World Championships, the Top 50 players in the Annual Top Finish Race not already qualified for Worlds will receive an invite to compete in that tournament.

Riftbound Grandmaster

At the conclusion of each year, starting with the end of 2027, the best 50 players according to the Annual Top Finish Race will be awarded the rank of Grandmaster for the following year.

Grandmasters are a subset of Platinum rank players, and will receive additional benefits. Two of which will be:

  • Free competitor badge to all Regionals
  • Free competitor badge and Day 2 qualification to all Continentals

Tokens

Tokens are not physical tokens. They are a digital reward in the play system which you can redeem. They are earned for finishes that are above defined thresholds for the type of event you’re competing in. Tokens are a tool for you to have some agency over which event you participate in, while keeping some predictability for participation in the event calendar as we plan the schedule.

This is essentially what we were already doing for the Top 64 competitors from each Regional Qualifier, we just didn’t have a formal name for it.

There are two types of tokens:

  1. Regional tokens.
    1. Regional tokens can be redeemed for a free competitor badge at one of the next 6 Regionals from when the token is earned.
  2. Continental Day 2 tokens.
    1. Continental Day 2 tokens can be redeemed for a free invite to Day 2 at one of the next 2 Continentals.

We're still finalizing policy around these tokens, and there are several situations we expect you to want to understand - such as, if you earn a token at an event, could you use it for an event the following weekend? Or the inverse: If there is an event the following weekend, would that count towards one of the six eligible events you can use your token at? Our team is working on these situations, and they'll be part of the full policy we release before the end of the year.

One of the changes that we are excited for is that the Challenge Series tournaments will offer Regional tokens, where the Summoner Skirmish events provided a bye.

Updated 2027 Regional & Continental Schedule

Here's the full schedule for Continental events in 2027. Below, we'll also get into the last Regional event for Legacy, plus the full regional schedule for The Reckoning. (Past that, there are a few 2027 Regionals that we're still locking in; we'll share the full details on those events at a later date.)

Continentals

These are the marquee events of our Organized Play structure. These tournaments will also be the largest tournament we run of the year, and are being hosted in venues larger than the largest Regional Qualifier events we held in 2026.

SetDatesCityVenueHashtag

Continentals are three-day events open to all, whereas this year's Regional Championships required players to have qualified to compete in them.

While we aren't ready to share full details on the Continentals' tournament structure, we know some of you will want to know how the open event and the Day 2 tokens will interact. The players who compete on Friday and make Day 2 will find their records reset as they are joined by players who have used Day 2 tokens.

We'll dive into this more as we get closer to the event.

Regionals

Regional Qualifiers did a massive amount of work for Riftbound this year, driving excitement and providing regular major tournaments for the community to attend, compete, watch, and rally around. We're not dramatically increasing the number of Regionals going into 2027, but we're increasing the size of these events in very real ways:

  • Three-Day Tournaments - Regionals move from only Saturday & Sunday to be Friday-Sunday. (More on this after the schedule.)
  • Larger Venues - Every Regional in 2027 is being held in spaces larger than regionally comparable RQs from 2026.

Here is our Regional schedule up through the middle of 2027:

Three-Day Tournament Structure

For 2026, one recurring reality was that Regional Qualifiers were long days of competition. We give huge thanks to the competitors for battling through those long days. Going into 2027, we are moving to start Regional Qualifiers on Friday.

Doing this allows us to make both Friday and Saturday 7 rounds of play, with a top cut for Sunday. You will need a 5-2 record (or better) at the end of Friday to come back and play on Saturday, where you'll compete to advance to Sunday.

The expansion of the tournament to three days does not mean Thursday now becomes an open hall day. We are finalizing logistics, but you should expect Thursday to be for picking up badges and purchasing merch (when the venue permits layouts that allow it outside the main hall).

This impacts things like the Pre-Regionals events, which were mainstays of this year's RQ schedules. We are not moving away from side events, they will remain a major part of these events. As we get closer to our first Regional in Legacy we'll share more information.

Best-Of Prizing

Recently we announced a change in prizing for the 2026 Regional Championships. This change caused many to have questions regarding both those changes and the future of Best-Of prizing. 

In addition to these questions, there were also many posts understandably expressing frustration over the timing of the changes.

Regarding the timing of the news, the frustration is completely justified—it would have been better to announce these changes earlier. We regret we weren’t able to make this happen and acknowledge the frustration that caused players. 

As for the concerns about the future of Best-Ofs, we want to reassure you that this pivot for the Regional Championships does not signify us moving away from Best-Of prizing altogether. We still see it as a powerful element of our competitive tournaments and intend to continue it into the future.

That said, we are continuing discussions about if the implementation may change. Many ideas have been levied by the community and by our teams and we are discussing what, if any, changes we should make to these plans.

Showdown Series

Showdown Series events are continuing to grow as part of our competitive programs for next year. We are looking to dramatically increase the number of these events for each set’s season, with an aim to deliver in the range of 30-40 each season, and have them provide global coverage to enable more players around the world to play competitive Riftbound and earn Ladder Points.

Additionally, the Regional and Continental Day 2 tokens system is a major step up in how we tie these programs into our larger competitive program, with roughly twice as many players each Showdown being fed into Day 2 of the Continentals than there were for Showdown invites for the Regional Championships.

The tier system for the Showdown Series is based on the number of competitors participating (not solely badges sold):

  • Tier 1: 512+ players
  • Tier 2: 256-511 players
  • Tier 3: 129-255 players

Due to the nature of Showdown Series events, we can’t unveil the schedule for next year, as they will continue to be announced on a rolling basis as we sign contracts and those partners prepare to share the events. 

To stay up to date on the Showdown Series offerings, the Roadmap articles will be kept up to date, but the most frequently updated resource will be RiftboundOP.com.

Challenge Series

The foundation of our competitive ladder is the new Challenge Series, which we announced in the August State of Play. This is the only event type run by local game stores that can offer Ladder Points and Regional tokens for players. As such, these tournaments are not going to be available to every store in the Riftbound Gaming Network. UVS has been working to identify stores around the world which qualify for hosting these events.

The winner of these events will get a stamped Promo and a Riftbound Regional token. Keep an eye out for these tournaments to begin popping up on the Riftbound Gaming Network in 2027!

Region Specific Competitive Series

In Riftbound's first year, we've made an effort to launch regional events such as France's Le Rift Tour, the Korea Tour, and the Taiwan RQ.

Both Korea and Taiwan are still early in Riftbound's local launch, and not yet up to parity for set releases. The region specific programs will continue into 2027, with a limited number of invitations for the top competitors of each program to the 2027 World Championship.

China, as the country where Riftbound was first launched, occupies a unique position in the Riftbound system. We are working to more tightly link their system into the global program but, for now, we intend China's events to largely work as they did in 2026; one notable change is that Majors will award invites for the 2027 World Championship.

Riftbound World Championship Showcase

Lastly, let's talk about the peak of competition. The 2026 World Championship Showcase is happening January 23-24, 2027 in Shanghai, China. 24 of the best Riftbound players in the world will come together and compete to crown the game's first World Champion. Like our other programs, the World Championship will also be changing after its first year.

The 2027 World Championship, fueled by the more robust competitive system we've been discussing, will be a larger event and tournament. Invites will be awarded to:

  • Every Regional winner.
  • Every Continental Top 8 finisher.
  • Every China Major winner.
  • Top finishers at the 2027 China Regional Championship event.
  • The Top 50 not already invited players according to Annual Finish ranking.
  • Top finishers for the Korea and Taiwan regional tournaments.

We've still got a lot of time between now and crowning our second World Champion, but it'll be exciting to see the roster of competitors grow as the year goes on.

PlayRiftbound.com

2027's play program underlines the importance of the new PlayRiftbound.com and why we launched it this year. You will begin seeing elements of this new program, tracking Ladder Points, ranking on the Ranked Ladder, and more as updates are pushed to the website in 2027. While those are implemented, we will communicate in the beginning of the year how to track these in the interim. As with this entire launch, it will continue to grow as the year progresses.

We are incredibly excited to see how Riftbound's first year winds up at the Regional Championships and the World Championship Showcase next year. And we're very eager for players to begin climbing the ladder!

FAQ

Q: What if...?

An article like this is sure to drive many questions about situations that could arise. We'll look at holding some AMAs or other community engagement opportunities in the future, but please feel free to share them online.

We ask you to please be patient as there will be many more questions than we can answer, and we'll work to get your questions answered.

Q: When will we know the remaining events for 2027?

We expect to announce the complete schedule for Regionals and Continentals before the end of 2026. (It may be towards the end...)

Q: Will my finishes in 2026 carry over into a rank for 2027?

No. We considered having the events of 2026 seed ranks for 2027, but ultimately decided against it for a few reasons. First, it felt unfair to surprise you with ranks you didn't know you were playing for. Additionally, given this year's transition to the PlayRiftbound.com system, we did not want to have any part of the competitive ranks rely on migrated data which may not be correct.

However, players who do have Top 64 finishes from a Regional Qualifier or equivalent finish from a Radiance Showdown Series which occur in 2027 will be honored.

Q: What Ladder Point totals are needed for each rank?

This is one where we have not finalized the numbers, and we don't want to give the initial values for the rank thresholds only to change them in the coming weeks. We'll share more in the future.

Q: What about Summoner Skirmish byes?

We dive into Summoner Skirmish sunsetting and what you need to know about it in the other article today.

Riftbound uses a drawing system for purchasing certain products from the Riot Merch Store. Here’s the details:

  • If your name is drawn, you’ll be sent a link to purchase a few days later via email. If you would like to purchase the products you selected, you’ll have a 24-hour window to do so.

  • If you decide not to purchase, or the time window expires and you haven’t completed your purchase, someone new will be drawn and notified.
  • Players should ensure that riotgames.com emails are not being marked as spam or filtered into the trash.
  • Players should check that they have access to their account prior to the sign up period for the drawing. If not they can visit Riot’s recovery platform or submit a ticket to player support.

If your name is chosen in the drawing, you’ll be sent a link to a shopping cart with the products that your name was drawn for. The link to purchase will work for 24 hours. If you choose not to purchase, we will move on to the next person, chosen at random.

You are able to remove items from your shopping cart if you do not wish to purchase all products which you were drawn for. Removing an item from your cart is final and cannot be undone.

What happens if someone is drawn but doesn’t purchase their product?

If a player is chosen to purchase one or more products but decides not to, that player’s chance at the bundle will be done as soon as their purchase window expires. 

Once a player’s purchase window expires, the stock will be returned to the store and the system will do a new drawing for the product that was not purchased. This drawing will only be drawn from among people who have not yet been selected for those products. These waves will continue until the stock on the Riot Merch store is depleted.

How do I receive product?

Once you’ve purchased the items you drew, they will begin fulfillment the day of the product’s wide release.

If you have feedback or run into issues or have questions, reach out to our Player Support team.

art.title: Testing Start of Game Rules
art.desc: We’re testing out some rule adjustments to equalize win rates between going first and second.
art.html:
We’ve had an exciting first year of Riftbound, and we’ve learned a lot within the last year. One thing hasn't changed—we’re committed to adapting to make the game better and more engaging for everybody. 

With that said, going first in turn order currently has a higher win rate than we would like, and along with the upcoming templating and rules overhaul planned for Legacy, we want to further improve the Riftbound playing experience by potentially making some adjustments here as well. We’ve landed on three possible changes that will get us closer to a 50% win rate split between going first and second. 

In order to evaluate which solution is best, we’ll be testing some new rules at events worldwide (outside of premier tournaments).

Is this a rules update? Do I have to follow the stuff in this article at my Nexus Night, or in my next match at Regionals?

No. Right now, we’re playtesting changes at select events to even out the win rate between going first vs. going second. 

Some of these changes may be finalized as part of Riftbound’s core ruleset, but we’re looking to get more data on which of our possible solutions works best before we make that call.

So, what are the changes you’re testing?

The current problem: going first in turn order has a higher win rate than we would like. This means that channeling an extra Rune—our current bonus for going second in turn order, or “go-second advantage”—isn’t enough of a boost to balance out the inherent advantage of going first.

Here’s what we’ll be testing to address this. Again, this is just a test for now. We’ll determine what changes make it to Riftbound’s actual ruleset after testing is finished.

  1. We’re changing turn order decisions to occur before Battlefields are selected. After battlefields are selected, sideboarding occurs if applicable, and then Battlefields are revealed.
    1. We want the choice to go first or second to be a solid commitment before your opponent's Battlefield is disclosed.
    2. In best-of-threes you will now be able to make every battlefield choice with the knowledge of who is going first or second.
    3. In best-of-one battlefield selection will remain random, but you will know which of your battlefields was selected before sideboarding. Your opponent’s will be revealed after sideboarding. 
    4. This means sideboarding decisions can be made with full knowledge of your turn order and your battlefield. This eliminates the added layer of considering your card selection and battlefield without knowing whether or not your opponent will choose to go first or second in the latter rounds of a best-of-three.
  2. We’re adding another perk to the go-second advantage. While playtesting these new rules, the player who goes second will get one of the following, in addition to channeling three Runes on their first turn:
    1. They will start at 1 point. Or,
    2. They will draw an extra card. Or,
    3. They will predict before their first draw.

Basically, we’re investigating whether card advantage, card quality, or points will most impact the win rate on going first vs. going second. Event staff will communicate clearly before each event whether A, B, or C will be tested. 

Each of these proposed solutions has their own advantages and disadvantages, and we’d love to break down some of the thoughts behind each of them. 

Start at 1 point

The core disadvantage to going second is that you’re behind on point-scoring opportunities. In this world, the first player would start the game ahead on board development because they take the first turn, but the second player would be ahead on points as a counterbalance. This is the most extreme change that we’re interested in, but we think it’s valuable to test a change that directly interacts with the scoring system that is central to the going first advantage.

Draw an extra card

Having more cards than your opponent is an advantage in a card game, and many card games give an extra card to the player who goes second. This makes it more likely that the second player has the card they need when they need it, and the extra material also gives them an advantage in games that go long and come down to attrition. 

We explored the idea of taking away the first player’s draw on their first turn, but ultimately decided it would create too large of a change in how players needed to build their decks. Giving the second player an extra card draw keeps deckbuilding incentives fairly similar and rhymes nicely with giving them an extra Rune, so we’ve chosen to test this version.

Predict before first draw

This is a softer version of the previous rule. If getting a whole extra card is too much, we think it could be enough to let the second player control their first draw based on their opponent’s choice of Battlefield and first turn play. We think that the whole extra card is a more straightforward solution, but this is an alternative that we’d like to test in case the extra card ends up being too strong.

What does this look like in practice?

Here’s how you’ll start your games if you’re in a playtest session. (Also, with these proposed rules, the start of game procedure will be more closely aligned between best-of-one and best-of-three formats.)

Best-of-three

  1. Decide which player will go first or second. 
  2. Select Battlefields, and place them facedown.
  3. Sideboard (in the second and third games). 
  4. Reveal Battlefields. 
  5. Mulligan.
  6. Going first player channels 2, and draws 1.
  7. Going second player channels 3. Then they Predict 1, or draw an extra card, or start with 1 point. (New)

Best-of-one

  1. Decide which player will go first or second. 
  2. Randomly select Battlefields.
  3. Look at your own Battlefield, keeping it hidden from the opponent. (New)
  4. Sideboard. 
  5. Reveal Battlefields. 
  6. Mulligan.
  7. Going first player channels 2, and draws 1.
  8. Going second player channels 3. Then they Predict 1, or draw an extra card, or start with 1 point. (New)

In both best-of-one and best-of-three, you will now be able to sideboard with the knowledge of your own Battlefield and turn order, but not your opponent’s Battlefield. 

Where will the playtests happen?

We’ll be testing these adjustments at events worldwide outside of our premier tournaments. You can expect to see playtests at:

  • Radiance season City Tournaments in China.
  • Friday and Sunday Standard Challenges at the upcoming European Regional Championship in Stuttgart.

We’ll be in touch with tournament officials about the logistics, and the rules being tested will be communicated to all participants attending the events. 

If you are interested in testing these rules out in local or casual games, we encourage you to do so! We’ve got eyes across the community, and will monitor conversation and feedback. That said, you’re not required to change anything about the way you play until we make an official rules update. Skirmishes, Showdowns and other high OPL events should not playtest these rules unless directly communicated to Tournament Organizers. 

Why playtest at events?

Testing rules changes at larger scale events gives us a much bigger pool of data to work from. With way more players testing these changes, we can get a much better idea of which solutions bring us closer to a 50% win rate split between going first and second. 

Beyond the numbers, we want to make sure these proposed solves feel good to play with as well, and that’s where your feedback comes in! 

When will the playtested rules actually be in effect globally?

We’re planning to analyze and dive deeper into the data from the Radiance season to make a decision leading into the launch of our sixth set, Legacy. 

You can expect an official rules adjustment (or an announcement that there will be no changes) to be included in our Patch Notes for Legacy, along with our reasoning and findings. The community is incredibly important to us, and as we make these changes to help Riftbound grow, we’re excited to bring everyone along for the ride and include your input to help make the game we all love even better.

art.title: Regional Championships: Competitive Integrity & Prizing
art.desc: Adjustments to Regional Championship prizing and policy.
art.html:
We are less than one month away from the European Regional Championship, taking place in Stuttgart, Germany, and we want to update competitors with:

  • Changes to prizing plans for Regional Championship events, including how Overnumber Foil Plated Legends are being awarded.
  • Updates to the Competitive Integrity Policy for Regional Championship events.
  • A brief look at the 2026 Riftbound World Championship Showcase event.

Best-Of & Overnumber Foil Plated Legends

When we introduced Best-Of prizing in Houston, it quickly became an exciting part of competitive Riftbound. As players moved from Regional Qualifiers to Regional Championships, we wanted the rewards to grow alongside the level of competition, leading us to introduce Overnumbered Foil Plated Legends as Regional Championship Best-Of prizes.

Since then, we’ve been tracking how these rewards influence competitive decisions beyond simply encouraging players to represent their favorite Legends. After discussing the role we want these prizes to play in Riftbound, we’re making the following adjustments to Regional Championship prizing:

  • Overnumbered Foil Plated Legends will now reward overall tournament performance.
    • The top 58 finishers will draft from the available Overnumbered Foil Plated Legends in finishing order, beginning with 1st place and continuing until all 58 Legends have been selected.
  • Foil Plated Legends from Unleashed, Vendetta, and Radiance will become the new Best-Of rewards. These will be awarded to the highest finishing eligible player on their respective Legend.
    • Origins, Proving Grounds, and Spiritforged Legends will not be eligible for Foil Plated Legend Best-Of prizing at Regional Championships.
    • Players must still advance to Day 2 on their Legend to qualify for a Best-Of Foil Plated Legend.

These Best-Of Foil Plated Legends are the same versions offered through Regional Qualifiers. Due to the timing of this adjustment, Radiance Foil Plated Legends will not be available for distribution at these events. We are currently determining the best way to deliver them to their recipients and expect them to become available in January 2027.

We believe these changes ultimately better reward competitors and incentivize the type of competition we want to see as part of Regional Championship Tournaments.

Policy Updates

In addition to the above changes to prizing, we are taking some more steps to further the competitive integrity of Regional Championships. Here are the rules updates:

  • No Throwing Matches: Players may not ask for or offer match concessions at any point before or during these tournaments except in the cases outlined below.
  • No Deciding Matches After Time: If a match naturally ends in a draw due to time limits, players cannot attempt to randomly or arbitrarily determine a winner.
  • Open Decklists: Regional Championships will be played with open decklists. 

Tournament Rule 401.5.b. states that tournaments with a professional OPL can be run with open decklists. We will be requiring this for these tournaments and want players to know this ahead of the events, and more importantly, ahead of when they need to lock their decklists.

Permitted Actions & Exceptions

We understand that certain situations require flexibility in the above. The following situations remain permitted:

  • Tactical Game Concessions: Players may concede individual games within a match for strategic reasons (such as preserving time for Game 3). But they may not tactically concede a match-determining game.
  • Legitimate Extenuating Circumstances: Players facing genuine external circumstances, such as medical emergencies, may yield a match.
  • Intentional Draws (IDs): Intentional Draws prior to time expiring remain legal and permitted under standard tournament policy.

Enforcement and Penalties

We will be reiterating these rules before each event, including in email to competitors and through tournament floor announcements.

Players are expected to play each match to the best of their ability with the intention of winning the match. Any player found asking for, offering, or executing illegal match concessions or collusion agreements will face immediate disqualification from the event and potential suspension from competitive Riftbound play.

2026 Riftbound World Championship Showcase Event

Lastly, we know that Overnumbered Foil Plated Legend cards have been the main motivation for many competitors at Regional Championships. With the 2026 Riftbound World Championship Showcase Event, the highest-level players will have something new to set their sights on, and Regional events are a crucial stepping stone to crowning our first World Champion. 

The Top 8 of each Regional Championship (Europe, North America, and China) will be invited to compete in Riftbound’s first World Championship Showcase event, taking place at the end of January in China. If someone manages the impressive feat of making Top 8 at multiple Regional Championships, any invitations earned beyond their first will be passed down to the next eligible finisher of the relevant tournament. 

We will share more about the World Showcase and what players will be competing for in future updates!

Lisez la suite pour découvrir ce que Riftbound prépare pendant l'événement.

Informations sur l'événement

Du 22 au 25 octobre 2026
Où : Paris Expo Porte de Versailles (1 place de la Porte de Versailles, 75015 Paris, France)
Site de l'événement : parisgamesweek.com/fr

Les participants qui assistent à un événement « Apprendre à jouer » dans la zone de démonstration pourront recevoir la carte promo d'événement Riven, Brisée.

22-25 octobre, 9h30-18h30 (CEST)

Le plus important : ne manquez pas la finale en direct du Rift Tour, le circuit compétitif officiel Riftbound de France, le samedi 24 octobre à 9h CEST.

Musée Radiance

Vous souhaitez voir Radiance plus en détail ? Visitez le musée au stand Riftbound, qui expose chaque carte de la nouvelle extension.

Cabine photo

Prenez une photo avec des amis et gardez un instantané de votre week-end.

Création personnalisée

Créez et imprimez votre propre création personnalisée pour ajouter une touche personnelle à votre prochain plateau. 

Rencontres avec les cosplayers

Le stand Riftbound accueillera une sélection en rotation de cosplayeurs autour du stand et sur scène. Venez faire un tour et prendre une photo avec vos champions préférés. 

Avec :

  • Kairi - @kairi_ahri
  • Marion - @sakusha_cos

Suivez les réseaux sociaux de Riftbound pour connaître les dates et horaires actualisés.

Le stand Riftbound à la Paris Games Week proposera des produits scellés Riftbound à la vente, y compris le tout nouveau bundle Secret Garden. 

Produits Riftbound

  • Boosters de Vendetta en français
  • Decks de confrontation Vendetta Zed vs Shen
  • Coffres-forts de Vendetta
  • Coffres-forts de Radiance

  • Secret Garden

art.title: Preparing for the Radiance Pre-Rift
art.desc: Get ready to play Riftbound’s newest set at your local Pre-Rift.
art.html:
Hello Riftbounders!

This Friday, October 16, stores will begin running their Radiance Pre-Rift events. 

Events begin on Friday, but the Pre-Rift window lasts for the week, so check the schedule at your local store to find out when you can register to play. If you want to see when local game stores are running Pre-Rifts near you, check out our event locator.

So, what’s a Pre-Rift event?

A Pre-Rift event is your first chance to get your hands on a new set’s cards and play with them before the set is officially released. When you attend a Pre-Rift, you get to crack packs with your local game store (LGS) community, build a deck, and play it immediately.

Pre-Rift events are fun, social, and casual! The focus is on learning and lighthearted fun, so don’t worry about bumping into any extreme competition. Instead, have fun with the people around you, chat about the deck you’re gonna try out, and don’t hesitate to ask your fellow Riftbounders or the event judge for help while you’re building your deck or in the middle of a game.

The other great thing about Pre-Rifts is that they are Sealed events. This means all the cards you need to play will be provided to you as part of the event, and you’ll just need to build your deck from that limited card pool.

What’s a Sealed format?

In Sealed formats, you open Booster Packs and play with the cards you get; for this event, they'll be Radiance Booster Packs. You can use any of the cards you open from those packs when building your deck, but you can’t add outside cards from your collection to your deck. 

If this is your first Sealed event, here are the deckbuilding rules to keep in mind: 

  • Sealed decks have a minimum Main Deck size of 25 cards, but you can play more than that if you want to.
  • Sealed decks can use up to three domains of cards and Runes. 
    • You can use any Signature spell in your deck, as long as both of that Signature spell’s domains are represented in your Main Deck’s three domains.  
  • You can choose to play without a Legend, or without a Champion Unit. If you do, you draw an additional card on your first turn.
    • If you choose to play with a Legend, you must have both of the Legend’s domains represented in your Main Deck’s three domains. 
  • You can use any Champion Unit as your Chosen Champion, regardless of your Legend.
  • You can use as many copies of a card as you open.
    • This means you can go above the normal limit of 3 copies per card.
  • You are not limited to using Runes or tokens that you open in your packs. 
    • The event organizer will provide additional Runes, and you can use anything handy to represent tokens! 
  • You can use Battlefields that you open, or use a facedown card as a "blank" substitute Battlefield. These blank Battlefields have no abilities and are just locations for players to conquer and hold. 
  • You can change the cards of your deck in between games and rounds, as long as you’re still following the other rules above. Don’t be afraid to alter your build as you go!
  • For more details on Sealed deckbuilding, see the Tournament Rules.

Pre-Rift Kit Contents

For Radiance Pre-Rift events, you’ll be provided with the following to open and use to build your deck. Remember, anything you open is yours to keep!

  • Five Radiance Booster Packs.
  • A champion pack themed around one of nine new Legends in Radiance. These packs have a Legend, a Rare Champion, a Battlefield, and support cards all for that Champion.
  • A Heimerdinger, Academy Instructor promo card. You can’t include the Heimerdinger Promo in your Sealed deck. If you pull the non-promo version in your packs, you can play that one! 

Building Your Deck

Remember, your Main Deck has to have at least 25 cards and follow the Domain rules listed above. With that in mind, here are a few tips for building your Sealed deck at a Pre-Rift:

  1. Include a reasonable amount of Units in your deck, because they’re  your main way to score points. 
    1. Most decks want to have at least 15 Units that can fight for you. 
    2. You’ll want about five of your Units to cost 2 Energy, so you have plays to make in your first turns. 
    3. The rest of your Units can be more expensive, with a diversity of costs so you have powerful plays at all points of the game.
  2. Use your non-Unit cards to help bolster the strategy of your deck. 
    1. Gear or Spells that give Might are great options to improve your Units. 
    2. It’s also always a good idea to have a few spells that will let you interact directly with your opponent’s Units by removing them from play.
  3. Think about the different Power costs in your deck. 
    1. Cards with Power costs tend to have stronger effects, and you will want to have some without going overboard on the Runes you'll have to recycle. 
    2. When deciding what Runes to play in your Rune Deck, make sure to think about the specific Power costs in your Main Deck.
  4. Radiance has new mechanics called Disarm, Deploy, and Show Off. 
    1. Try playing around with the new keywords to learn how they work.

When building the foundation of your deck, the cards from your Pre-Rift kit are a great place to start. Here's a quick rundown on the Champions in the Pre-Rift kits and their strategies. 

Pre-Rift Seeded Legends

 Ekko

Ekko is all about planning ahead, and manipulating time. Use his Legend to cheat out powerful units with impactful effects ahead of the curve. 

Evelynn

Evelynn is all about luring you into her embrace and springing her trap. She uses hidden cards to outwit her enemies. 

Jarvan IV

Jarvan IV leverages the new keyword Deploy. With his Legend, you can send Units to battlefields with Deployed Gear and surprise your opponent, getting Units directly into the fight even if your base is empty. You can’t count Jarvan out of the fight. 

K’Sante

K’Sante is all about protecting his allies and Battlefields. His unique flavor is that he can transform his defenses to be used on offense. Surprise your opponents by turning your beefy Hold cards into Conquering monsters.

Modekaiser

Mordekaiser rules over the realm of death. His game plan centers around banishing his own Gear and Units, to play out more Units and Gear for cheaper.

Orianna

Orianna’s Legend puts a new spin on Riftbound. She can transform powerful Gear into powerful Units, and even surprise opponents by transforming Deployed Gear into a Unit at unexpected times. Use your robot army to conquer Battlefields from underneath the opponent’s nose.

Riven

Riven is an exiled swordfighter who focuses on movement, and her Legend leans into this game plan. Allowing Units that are played to the Battlefield to come in ready synergises with cards that can Gank or have exhaust abilities, creating a surprising amount of early game pressure.

Seraphine

Seraphine draws powers from her followers, and can exhaust them to help her cast expensive, game-changing spells. Her game plan is to assemble a large army of low cost Units and overwhelm her opponent with both spells and sheer numbers.

Ziggs

Ziggs is a chaotic yordle who wants to blow everything up—and he really wants to blow up the board. His game plan leans fully into controlling the board and deterring the enemy from even setting foot on a Battlefield. 

Pre-Rift Rules FAQ

If you haven't, check out our recently released patch notes. We’ll be releasing an extended FAQ once Radiance has been out for a bit to cover any odd interactions, but we wanted to call out a few things early to make Pre-Rift as smooth as possible.

Q: If I use K’Sante Legend on a Unit like Staunch Survivor that has both Shield 2 and Assault 2, does the card now have Assault 4?

A: Yes! This is worded this way to communicate that K’Sante’s Legend is a passive effect for that turn. This way you can use combat tricks to give that Unit additional Shield, and increase their Assault that turn! 

Q: If I pull Neeko and have fewer than 3 Legends, can I still play Neeko?

A: Yes, you can! Neeko is receiving an errata to read “...choose up to 3 different Legends...” so you can still legally play Neeko in Pre-Rift even if you don’t pull 3 Legends.

Q: Can I choose the same option twice when playing Encore? 
A: No, you cannot. You must choose 2 different options from the 4.

Q: When an Equipment becomes a unit, does it inherit its equipped text?
A: No. Its “Equipment” text is only active when it is equipped to a unit. If you are running Orianna Legend with a Blade of Exile in your deck and turn it into a Unit, it will be a 3 might Unit without Ganking. 

See You On the Rift!

Excited to find a nearby Pre-Rift? Check the event locator and find one near you—and don’t forget to post your hits! Tag us at @PlayRiftbound with the hashtag #RBRadiance.
